title: Unify credential extension points, introduce compact async-iterable facade, and align retry presets across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs
author: Priya Nair
body:
Summary: This PR harmonizes credential extension points and retry presets across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs and introduces a lightweight async-iterable facade to standardize streaming ergonomics. Motivation: teams have been implementing ad-hoc credential fallback and stream iteration logic per-language which causes subtle bugs during reauth, inconsistent backoff behavior, and doubles the maintenance surface. This change reduces duplication, improves cross-language parity, and makes migration to newer retry strategies straightforward.

What changed (high-level):
- Introduced a small, opinionated CredentialSynchronizer interface (language idioms: ContextManager for Python, CredentialAttendant for TS, CredentialOrchestrator for Go) and implementation hooks for delegated refresh, prefetch, and fanout.
- Added CompactAsyncIterable facade for streaming responses: provides a minimal, cancelable async iterator that supports pause/resume and a stable close/cleanup contract. Implemented in py/ts/go SDK entry points.
- Consolidated retry preset profiles into a single canonical set (fast_retries / balanced / conservative) and wired them into the SDK constructors and stream adapters. Presets are deterministic, test-covered, and documented.
- Small ergonomic API tweaks: clearer errors for credential failures, a single env var to opt-in to legacy vs new retry semantics (REDWOOD_SDK_RETRY_MODE), and explicit deprecation warnings for older credential hooks.
- Version bumps: python->1.9.0, typescript->2.6.0, go->v1.14.0; changelogs updated.

Checklist (done):
- [x] Design doc reviewed with SDK leads (ENG-8125)
- [x] Implementations for all three SDKs
- [x] Unit + integration tests for token rotation and stream cancellation
- [x] Basic interop e2e across hosted API (small script)
- [x] Migration notes in each SDK CHANGELOG

Testing and CI notes: All SDK builds pass on CI. The change required small parallelization tweaks in the python integration suite to avoid token-bus contention; CI workflow updated to use isolated fixtures when running interop tests. There is an additional flaky test (TS stream-reconnect) that was stabilized by increasing socket timeout; we've tracked the original flaky CI run in SUP-1478.

Backward compatibility and migration guidance: This PR aims to be non-breaking. Existing credential hooks will continue to work, but will emit a deprecation warning if they rely on the legacy reauth callback signature (old_signature: (ctx) -> token). Migration steps are documented in the CHANGELOGs and examples folder. For teams that cannot migrate immediately, set REDWOOD_SDK_RETRY_MODE=legacy to preserve prior retry timing.

Performance/behavior notes: Standardizing retry presets reduces end-to-end token refresh storms under burst load; internal perfbench across a simulated webhook workload showed a 18% reduction in auth-related request latency variance and a 12% reduction in token refresh RPCs per minute.

Files of interest (high-level): sdks/python/redwood_sdk/auth/synchronizer.py; sdks/python/redwood_sdk/stream/compact_iterable.py; sdks/typescript/src/auth/attendant.ts; sdks/typescript/src/stream/compactIterable.ts; sdks/go/credentials/orchestrator.go; sdks/go/stream/compact_iterable.go; ci/workflows/sdk-integration.yml; docs/sdks/migration/credential_and_retry.md

Release notes: Introduce CredentialSynchronizer and CompactAsyncIterable; align retry presets across SDKs; minor API ergonomics and version bumps (Python 1.9.0, TS 2.6.0, Go v1.14.0). No breaking changes by default; opt-in legacy mode available.

Why this is unique: Instead of a per-SDK one-off, this PR is a minimal cross-language contract + reference implementations approach — small surface area but high leverage for future SDK features (session caching, stream pooling, and observability hooks).

d4e7b1a: introduce CompactAsyncIterable interface across sdks
c8f1d55: align retry preset definitions and wire through constructors
e12a4b0: update changelogs and bump package versions
f99b622: ci: isolate integration fixtures to avoid token contention
review_comments: Diego Morales: Left a couple of nits in the TS attendant about edge-case cancellation; can we add an explicit unit test that calls .return() on the iterator path?
Priya Nair (author): Good catch, added ts test and clarified the return/cleanup contract in compactIterable.ts; included the test in the commit c8f1d55.
Ava Chen: The Go orchestrator looks good; one suggestion: rename StartPrefetch to Prime to match other orchestrator APIs. Not required for merge but would be nice for parity.
Priya Nair: Renamed StartPrefetch->Prime in a follow-up commit and added a tiny docstring, addressed the comment.
Liam O'Neill: Verified integration run locally with the hosted API; token rotation storm scenario behaved as expected and metrics improved. Approving.
post_merge_notes: Merged to main. SDK packages tagged and release pipelines triggered. Docs and examples updated. QA will run a canary for 48 hours on Dedicated customers before wider rollout.
release_notes: See release notes: CredentialSynchronizer + CompactAsyncIterable + retry preset alignment; SDK version bumps; non-breaking by default (REDWOOD_SDK_RETRY_MODE to opt into legacy behavior).
